1.title: Expressions, Functions, count, foreach and Dynamic Blocks
1.text: Welcome to Module seven: Expressions, Functions, count, for each and Dynamic Blocks. It covers the exam area four. Terraform configuration. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Expressions. Functions. count and for each. Dynamic blocks. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: four. Terraform configuration. Exam format: a one-hour online-proctored multiple-choice exam on Terraform one point one two. Validated against: the official Terraform Associate version oh oh four exam objectives.

1.title: Expressions
1.text: Expressions. An expression computes a value inside configuration. String template. Example: var dot name -web. Meaning: Insert a value into a string. Conditional. Example: var dot prod? large small. Meaning: Choose between two values. For expression. Example: for s in var dot names upper s. Meaning: Transform a list into a new list. For expression (map). Example: for k, v in var dot tags k upper v. Meaning: Build a map.

1.title: Expressions, continued
1.text: Expressions. Splat. Example: aws instance dot web dot id. Meaning: All the id values of a counted resource. Index. Example: var dot names zero, var dot tags Name. Meaning: One element.

1.title: Expressions, continued
1.text: Expressions. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: for... builds a list; for... builds a map; is the splat. The conditional has three parts: condition, true value, false value.

1.title: Functions
1.text: Functions. Terraform has built-in functions (and provider-defined functions from providers); you cannot write your own functions in H C L. You call them as name arguments. String. upper, lower, format, join, split, replace, trimspace. Collection. length, concat, merge, lookup, keys, values, flatten, element, contains. Numeric. min, max, ceil, floor. Type conversion. tolist, toset, tomap, tostring, tonumber. Filesystem. file, templatefile, fileexists. Network. cidrsubnet, cidrhost. Error handling. try, can, coalesce. Use terraform console to try expressions and functions interactively against your configuration and state. Exam tip: merge combines maps, concat joins lists, lookup reads a map with a default, length counts. terraform console is the place to test an expression.

1.title: count and foreach
1.text: count and for each. Both create several instances of a resource or module from one block. Input. count: A number. for each: A map or a set of strings. Instance index. count: A number: aws instance dot web zero. for each: A key: aws instance dot web a. Inside the block. count: count dot index. for each: each dot key, each dot value. Removing an item. count: May shift the numbers and replace other instances. for each: Only the removed key is affected. Use when. count: Identical copies. for each: Copies that differ or stable names.

1.title: count and foreach, continued
1.text: count and for each. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: count and foreach, continued
1.text: count and for each. count and for each cannot be used together on one block. Exam tip: Prefer for each when the items have identity, because removing one item does not renumber the rest. for each needs a map or a set, not a list.

1.title: Dynamic blocks
1.text: Dynamic blocks. A dynamic block generates repeated nested blocks (for example several ingress rules) from a collection. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Dynamic blocks, continued
1.text: Dynamic blocks. dynamic ingress. The nested block type to repeat. for each. The collection to loop over. content. The body of each generated block. ingress dot value. The current item (named after the block label). Exam tip: Use dynamic for repeated nested blocks inside a resource; use count or for each for repeated resources.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A team needs three identical virtual machines from one resource block. Which meta-argument is simplest? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: count. count creates a number of identical instances from one block.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A configuration creates a bucket for each name in a set of names. Which meta-argument fits and what is referenced inside? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: for each with each.key. for each creates one instance per element, and each.key and each.value refer to the current element.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which expression returns a list with every name converted to upper case? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A for expression in square brackets that applies upper to each name. A for expression in square brackets builds a new list from the transformed elements; curly braces would build a map.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which function combines two maps into one? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: merge. merge combines maps; concat joins lists.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A security group needs one ingress block for every port in a list that can change. What should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A dynamic block with for each. A dynamic block generates repeated nested blocks from a collection.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which command lets an engineer test an expression against the configuration and state interactively? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: terraform console. terraform console evaluates expressions and functions interactively.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does the splat expression return? Answer: The attribute from every instance of a counted resource. Question two. Which function reads the length of a list? Answer: length. Question three. What inputs can for each take? Answer: A map or a set of strings.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Can count and for each be used together? Answer: No. Question five. What does a dynamic block generate? Answer: Repeated nested blocks. Question six. Can you define your own function in H C L? Answer: No; there are built-in and provider-defined functions.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Expressions: template, conditional (condition? a: b), for (list or map), splat, index. Functions: built-in (and provider-defined): merge (maps), concat (lists), lookup, length, try; terraform console. count or for each: number or map or set; count.index or each.key and each.value. dynamic: repeated nested blocks: for each plus content.
